questions.q: What is the core risk of a single EOA controlling a contract's owner functions or deploy/upgrade authorization?
options: It costs more gas than a multisig
It's one leaked private key, phished signer, or compromised device away from total loss of control
It can't be used with Foundry
It makes the contract immutable
questions.explain: A single key is a single point of failure — compromise it once, and whoever holds it controls everything it's authorized to do.

questions.q: What does an "M-of-N" threshold on a Safe account mean?
options: M total owners, N signatures required
N total owners, M signatures required before a transaction executes
The Safe can only be used N times
M is the gas limit and N is the block number
questions.explain: M-of-N means N total owners exist, and M of them must sign a transaction before it actually executes — e.g. 4 of 7.

questions.q: In the real Safe{Wallet} queue screenshot shown in this lesson, what does a pending transaction's confirmation count (e.g. "1 out of 4") represent?
options: The transaction's position in the block
How many of the required owner signatures have been collected so far for that specific transaction
The number of times the transaction has failed
The gas price multiplier
questions.explain: Each pending transaction tracks its own confirmation progress toward the Safe's threshold — nothing executes until enough owners confirm.

questions.q: Does a Safe account ever hold or have access to an individual owner's private key?
options: Yes, Safe stores all owner keys centrally for recovery purposes
No — each signer manages their own key independently; the Safe only requires enough of their signatures
Only for the Safe's primary admin owner
Only when using the mobile app
questions.explain: A Safe is a smart contract requiring signatures from independently-held owner keys — it never custodies any individual owner's private key itself.

questions.q: How does the lesson describe wiring a Safe into a deployment pipeline?
options: The deploy script broadcasts directly with no human involvement, same as a single-key deploy
A deploy/upgrade transaction is proposed to the Safe, then the required number of owners confirm it through Safe{Wallet} before it executes on-chain
Every team member must independently redeploy the same contract
Safe cannot be used for contract deployments, only for token transfers
questions.explain: The lesson describes a propose-then-confirm flow: a transaction is proposed to the Safe (e.g. by CI), and enough owners must confirm it before it actually executes.
